skill.summary: Understand your readers through their questions, language, and observed engagement.

content.user_title: Identify Your Readers from Real Responses
content.value_statement: Fictional personas can distract writers from the questions real readers ask. This skill uses engagement, reader responses, and posts to identify audience questions and vocabulary.
actual_capabilities: Prioritize evidence from people who engage, their responses, and posts grouped by subject.
Produce six to ten reader questions using language from actual responses when enough evidence exists.
Compare reader vocabulary with the terms used in your writing.
Identify existing reading sources, followed accounts, and conversations when evidence supports them.
Describe evidence gaps and label audience conclusions as provisional when samples are small.
Use available VoiceMOAT analytics, posts, and voice insights to support topic and vocabulary comparisons.
limitations: Requires existing reader evidence and stops rather than inventing an audience when none exists.
Does not infer age, income, lifestyle, or seniority beyond observed job titles.
Does not create fictional named personas or guarantee that engagement represents every reader.
Optional VoiceMOAT access requires a connected account on the Pro or Enterprise plan.

use_cases.title: Plan Posts Around Reader Questions
use_cases.description: Turn real comments and replies into recurring questions and compare audience vocabulary with the language used in published posts.

use_cases.title: Investigate Audience Mismatch
use_cases.description: Review who engages and which subjects receive responses to distinguish the observed audience from the audience a business hoped to reach.

use_cases.title: Review Topic Performance
use_cases.description: Use connected VoiceMOAT posts and analytics to group subjects and compare reactions relative to impressions rather than raw counts.
use_cases.target_user: Content strategists and social media managers

prompt_templates.title: Identify Initial Reader Questions
prompt_templates.prompt: Here are my posts and reader comments: [evidence]. What questions are readers asking? Use their wording and state where evidence is missing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand a small set of reader responses.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reader and Writer Vocabulary
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these posts [posts] with these responses [responses]. List reader terms beside my terms and explain mismatches without inventing audience traits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: align writing with observed reader language.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an Audience Mismatch
prompt_templates.prompt: I intend to reach [audience]. Review [posts, responses, and engagement evidence]. Identify observed reader questions, supported audience differences, and evidence gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess whether actual engagement matches an intended audience.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Connected Evidence Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my authorized VoiceMOAT connection to review posts, analytics, and voice insights. Combine these with [reader responses]. Group subjects and compare reactions relative to impressions. Produce six to ten evidence-based questions, vocabulary comparisons, and provisional conclusions. Identify existing reader conversations only when supported.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine available connector data with supplied reader responses.

output_examples.input: Two readers ask, 'Does this work with no budget?' and 'What if we have no designer?' Our post describes 'resource-efficient creative operations.'
output: Reader questions: Does this work with no budget? What if we have no designer?
Vocabulary comparison: readers say 'no budget' and 'no designer'; the post says 'resource-efficient creative operations.'
Evidence strength: provisional, based on two responses. Collect more comments and compare responses across subjects before expanding the question list.

output_examples.input: Connected analytics show tutorial posts received 100 reactions across 2,000 impressions. Opinion posts received 150 reactions across 10,000 impressions.
output: Tutorial posts: 5% reactions relative to impressions. Opinion posts: 1.5%.
Tutorials have the higher reaction rate despite fewer total reactions.
Reader questions and vocabulary remain unknown without responses. These figures do not establish reader demographics.

best_practices: Provide representative posts and actual responses, with sensitive personal details removed.
Keep reader wording intact and separate directly observed facts from unsupported audience assumptions.
Group posts by subject and report sample size, missing evidence, and provisional conclusions.
anti_patterns: Inventing demographics, lifestyles, or named characters to make audience research appear complete.
Treating follower counts or raw reaction totals as proof of reader needs.
Presenting a few comments as a complete audience picture without stating uncertainty.

faq.question: What evidence should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide posts, comments, replies, messages, and available engagement data. Focus on people who engage rather than only on followers.

faq.question: Can this skill create a traditional persona?
faq.answer: It produces reader questions and vocabulary comparisons instead of a fictional profile. It does not invent demographics or named characters.

faq.question: What happens when I have no reader responses?
faq.answer: The skill states that evidence is missing and stops rather than inventing a persona. Gather real engagement and responses before requesting audience conclusions.

faq.question: Do I need VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: No. You can supply evidence directly. Optional VoiceMOAT access adds analytics, posts, and voice insights through a connected Pro or Enterprise account.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Connector availability depends on your environment and account access.

faq.question: How reliable are conclusions from a small sample?
faq.answer: Conclusions remain provisional when evidence is limited. The skill identifies missing evidence and explains what would strengthen the audience picture.
